en: The Sūtra on the Fifty Conditions for the Bodhisattva’s Practice of the Body,
translated by the Tripitaka Master Zhu Fahu of the Yuezhi during the Western Jin Dynasty.
At that time, the Buddha was staying on Vulture Peak near Rājagṛha, together with a community of twelve hundred bhikṣus.

One hundred and fifty people—bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, and upāsikās—as well as countless devas, nāgas, and spirits, and one hundred thousand bodhisattvas who had come from the ten directions, all sat spontaneously upon lion thrones made of seven-jeweled lotuses.
The bodhisattvas from the ten directions beheld the Buddha’s incomparable majesty and comeliness; his body was endowed with the thirty-two major marks and eighty minor characteristics.
Among those seated there was a bodhisattva named Jñānaśrī, who addressed the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī, saying:
“O Virtuous One!...”
"Knowing the profound sutras, one can understand for oneself by what causes and conditions the Buddha adorns his body and attains such merit.
When the bodhisattvas of the ten directions heard these words, there was none who did not rejoice.
Mañjuśrī immediately rose, knelt with his right knee on the ground before the Buddha, and addressed him, saying:

“Among the bodhisattvas in this assembly, there are those who have already attained *avaivartika* [the stage of non-retrogression] and those who have not yet attained *avaivartika*. All of them see the Buddha’s body adorned with the thirty-two marks and eighty secondary characteristics, its majesty so sublime that it is beyond compare.”
By what causes and conditions is this attained?
We pray that the Buddha will explain for the sake of the bodhisattvas the merits they performed in previous lives; upon hearing this, the bodhisattvas shall further increase their merit.
The Buddha said: “Excellent, excellent, Mañjuśrī!”
"To have conceived such an intention as to ask this!
The Buddha said,
"Listen as I relate the merits I cultivated in my previous lives."

"Throughout successive lifetimes, the Bodhisattva gave away whatever precious and rare objects he held dear; he constantly bestowed excellent vision and a benevolent mind. By virtue of this, the Buddha has attained all-encompassing wisdom that knows all sūtras and dharmas."

"Throughout successive lifetimes, the Bodhisattva maintained female attendants, rare treasures, and ornaments, and bestowed them upon others with a benevolent mind; by virtue of this, he attains the Buddha’s voice that emits ten thousand kinds of sounds."

“Throughout successive lifetimes, the Bodhisattva has always looked upon the people of the world with excellent vows and benevolent intentions. For this reason, when sentient beings behold the Buddha’s gaze, they never tire of it; it is like the full moon on the fifteenth day, beautiful and radiant, which one can gaze upon without ever reaching satiety.”

"Throughout successive lifetimes, the Bodhisattva has preached the Dharma to people without harboring any expectations, seeking only to bring them peace and security. For this reason, when the Buddha preaches the sutras, there are none among those who hear them who ever feels weary or satiated."

“Throughout successive lifetimes, the Bodhisattva does not speak of the faults of others, nor does he speak of those who have faults to others; for this reason, dust and defilements do not adhere to the Buddha’s body.”

“Throughout successive lifetimes, the Bodhisattva constantly endured insults and humiliation; though he possessed physical strength, he endured it all. For this reason, when the Buddha walks, the high ground becomes low and the low ground becomes high.”

"Throughout successive lifetimes, the Bodhisattva saw those in poverty and distress and provided them with sufficient aid; seeing those who were ruined or displaced, he restored them to their positions and brought them peace. For this reason, when the Buddha travels upon his path, the earth manifests its majestic power in a manner like that of joy."

"Throughout successive lifetimes, the Bodhisattva did not employ bows, crossbows, swords, or weapons to cause mutual harm among people. For this reason, when the Buddha travels, thorns, shards, stones, and ruins are all naturally cleared away."

"Because the Bodhisattva, throughout successive lifetimes, did not dare to violate or neglect the Dharma he heard from his teachers, for this reason, all the deeds performed by the Buddha are fully perfected in this way.

Because the Bodhisattva, throughout successive lifetimes, delighted in lighting lamps before Buddhist temples, teachers, and parents, and immediately resolved the doubts of those who were uncertain, for this reason, the radiance of the Buddha’s body issues forth in blazing flames; it is exceptionally beautiful beyond compare, and his majestic spiritual power is thus sublime."

"If, in life after life, a bodhisattva sees a slave or servant preaching the sutras and does not rebuke them to stop, but instead listens himself, for this reason the Buddha’s preaching of the sutras is free from stumbling or error."

"Throughout his successive lifetimes, the Bodhisattva did not look upon others with evil eyes; even when he experienced anger, he gradually endured it. For this reason, the Buddha’s eyes are neither too large nor too small, but are long and beautiful; there is no one who beholds the Buddha and does not feel joy."

“Throughout his successive lives, the Bodhisattva never harbored lustful intentions toward other people’s beautiful women; for this reason, the Buddha’s physical complexion is incomparably exquisite, and there is no one who beholds him who does not rejoice.”

"Throughout his successive lives, the Bodhisattva has offered seasonal fruits and fragrant flowers to the Buddhas, the community of bhikṣus, teachers, and parents. Because of this, whenever fruit trees and flowers see the Buddha, they all bend toward him in homage."

“Throughout his successive lives, the Bodhisattva sees mounds, ruins, and treacherous paths and makes them level and smooth; seeing places without bridges, he constructs bridges for them. He does not intimidate people for the sake of wealth or property. For this reason, when the Buddha enters through a low gate, it becomes great.”

"In every lifetime, wherever the Bodhisattva saw places that were desolate, empty, lacking wells, or devoid of trees, he would plant trees, dig wells, and provide various foods and drinks so that people might eat. Because of this, wherever the Buddha travels, springs gush forth from the earth, and the water possesses the eight qualities."

"Because the Bodhisattva, in life after life, did not speak of the faults of others when seeing them walking, entering, or exiting, for this reason the Buddha’s body is entirely beautiful and free from blemish.

Because the Bodhisattva, in life after life, applied blended incenses to the Buddha’s body and offered good intentions as gifts to the Buddha and to the high stupas, for this reason the devas and humans create fragrant winds to offer to the Buddha."

“Throughout successive lifetimes, the Bodhisattva offered various scented waters for the Buddhas and all Bodhisattvas to wash their faces, as well as willow branches for cleaning their teeth; because of this, the Buddha’s face and mouth are fragrant, like opening the seal of a treasure chest.”

“Throughout successive lifetimes, whenever a Bodhisattva saw someone harboring thoughts of anger toward him, he always treated that person with a kind heart. Because of this, when the Buddha walked along the road, not a single insect or ant beneath his feet failed to find peace and security; such is the majesty and sublimity of the Buddha’s awesome spiritual power.”

“Throughout successive lifetimes, the Bodhisattva offered all lands, as well as fine incense, flowers, robes, and coverlets to the Buddhas. Because of this, when someone scatters flowers upon a Buddha, they immediately form a flower-canopy.”

“Throughout his successive lives, the Bodhisattva did not destroy the dwellings of others and always delighted in building houses for them. For this reason, the Buddha possesses a diamond-like strength as firm as the four mountains on all sides, such that no one is able to harm his body.”

"In every lifetime, whenever a Bodhisattva saw someone suffering from hunger or thirst, he would first provide them with food and drink, and afterwards preach the sutras for them. Because of this, wherever the Buddha dwells, there are always fragrant flowers and flowing water before him."

“Throughout successive lifetimes, whenever people come to the Bodhisattva seeking anything, he gives it to them immediately without any sense of attachment or stinginess. For this reason, when the Buddha preaches the sutras, those who hear them do not suffer in vain; all derive benefit. For this reason, the Buddha subdues all Māras.”

"Because the Bodhisattva, in life after life, provided excellent music to delight the Buddha and his stūpas, for this reason, when the Buddha preaches the sūtras for his disciples, all people throughout an entire Buddha-field hear them completely."

"Because the Bodhisattva, in life after life, has offered trees made of gold, silver, and various jewels to the Buddhas, for this reason, no devas, nāgas, ghosts, or spirits are able to see the crown of the Buddha's head."

"In every lifetime, the Bodhisattva constructed stūpas for the Buddhas and anointed them with various fragrant incenses; by virtue of this, wherever the Buddha travels, rare jewels, incense, and flowers are scattered upon him."

"Throughout his successive lifetimes as a bodhisattva, whenever he saw someone afflicted by poison, he would immediately go to heal them with a mind of loving-kindness. For this reason, wherever the Buddha goes, whether it be people or trees, he completely cures all those afflicted by poison."

“Throughout successive lifetimes, the Bodhisattva has always followed the sutras and the Dharma without transgression, and his mind is ever supple and patient toward others. For this reason, even when those who are deranged come to the Buddha’s presence, there are none who do not attain peace and security.”

“Because the Bodhisattva has, in life after life, constantly offered various kinds of incense as an offering to the Buddha’s relics and anointed the stupas, for this reason, the Buddha’s body has no foul odors, defects, or impurities; calamities cannot affect the Buddha’s body, and the majesty of the Buddha’s spiritual power is thus so sublime.”

"Throughout his successive lives, whenever people were plagued by doubt and confusion, or possessed by ghosts and spirits, the Bodhisattva would immediately go to rescue them and bring them to liberation. For this reason, wherever the Buddha goes, if there are insects or ants on the ground, he removes them all."

"In every lifetime, a bodhisattva serves his teachers, parents, and others; if he sees them lying down or asleep, he does not wake them abruptly. If he wishes to awaken them, he should do so by bringing music or pleasant words, or by reciting sutras as he approaches. For this reason, when the Buddha is within and remains silent, the devas, Brahmā, and Śakra bring music and incense to awaken him."

"Throughout successive lifetimes, the Bodhisattva built vihāras for the Buddhas and took great care in preparing their beds, bedding, and utensils; because of this, mosquitoes, gadflies, bees, snakes, fleas, and lice dared not approach the Buddha’s body."

"In life after life during the cold winters, this Bodhisattva has fashioned fine and exquisite robes for the Buddha and the various bodhisattvas; because of this, whenever the *lana* wind arises, he remains before the Buddha neither cold nor hot, and not even a single hair on his body moves."

"Throughout his successive lives, the Bodhisattva never ate exquisite and delicious food alone. If his teacher or parents had food, he would not eat it without first sharing with them. For this reason, even when the Buddha sets aside his majestic spiritual power and has nothing to eat, he neither suffers from hunger nor thirst, and his body does not grow weak."

“Throughout successive lifetimes, the Bodhisattva did not set fire to mountains or forests, nor did he remove the three poisons from others; for this reason, after the Buddha’s parinirvāṇa, although the flames were fiercely blazing, they could not cause the Buddha’s complexion to change.”

"Throughout successive lifetimes, the Bodhisattva has always offered his most excellent dwellings, clothing, and food to his teachers, parents, and those of moral virtue; and to those who came to beg from him, he gave whatever they requested. Because of this, the devas, spirits, and elders present all the rare treasures and household articles of the world to the Buddha."

"In every lifetime, the Bodhisattva prepared the Buddha's path by applying fragrant ointments to the ground; for this reason, when the Buddha walks upon the path, various beautiful flowers are scattered in rows upon the earth."

"Throughout successive lifetimes, the Bodhisattva maintained the precepts without ever transgressing them, nor did he ever instruct others to transgress. For this reason, even when the violent winds arise from the four directions, they cannot move a single hair of the Buddha."

"In every lifetime, when the Bodhisattva was practicing the Buddha-way, he offered five-colored canopies for the Buddhas and invited them, along with the community of bhikṣus, to take a meal beneath them. Because of this, wherever the Buddha travels, the devas unfurl five-colored canopies and follow after him; such is the majesty and sublimity of the Buddha’s spiritual power."

"In every lifetime, the Bodhisattva offered precious jewels and sandals to the Buddhas with a virtuous mind. Because of this, when the Buddha walks, his feet remain four inches above the ground without treading upon it, and the marks of his feet appear clearly."

"In every lifetime, the Bodhisattva held banners, streamers, and flowered canopies of various five colors and offered them to the Buddha’s stūpas; by virtue of this, naturally produced banners, streamers, and canopies of various colors arise and follow the Buddha as he travels."

"Throughout successive lifetimes, the Bodhisattva prepared the path for the Buddha by sprinkling it with a mixture of fragrant juices; for this reason, wherever the Buddha travels, the nāgas hold forth a mixture of fragrant juices and sprinkle the ground."

“Throughout his successive lifetimes, the Bodhisattva has never uttered impure words or speech that people loathe; even if such words were present, he would restrain his mind and refrain from speaking them. For this reason, the devas, nāgas, spirits, and flying birds do not pass over the Buddha.”

"Throughout successive lifetimes, whenever a Bodhisattva sees a Buddha or a community of bhikṣus approaching, he rises to welcome them and pays homage to the Buddha. Because of this, wherever the Buddha travels, none among the devas, Brahmās, Śakras, asuras, ghosts, spirits, or the people of the world fail to welcome the Buddha, bowing their heads to touch his feet."

“Throughout successive lifetimes, the Bodhisattva constantly guards his body, speech, and mind, refraining from committing any evil deeds. He does not merely act with his body; rather, he practices giving for the sake of all people throughout the ten directions. Because of this, when the Bodhisattva is in his mother’s womb, foul odors and impurities do not touch his body; he remains always peaceful and secure, free from fear, and no one can cause him harm.”

"Throughout successive lifetimes, the Bodhisattva maintains a benevolent mind toward the Buddha; whether seeing an enemy or seeing his parents, his mind remains perfectly equanimous without any distinction. For this reason, the Buddha’s wisdom is fully perfected, consisting solely of all that is wholesome and devoid of anything unwholesome; when people have doubts or difficulties, there is nothing the Buddha cannot resolve."

“Because the Bodhisattva, in lifetime after lifetime, offered various musical instruments, diverse incenses, and flowers to the Buddhas and their stūpas, for this reason, when the Buddha enters the city, all the musical instruments within the city sound spontaneously without being struck.”

“Throughout successive lifetimes, the bodhisattva maintains gold, silver, precious jewels, and other treasures—whether they be flawless, inferior, or of mixed quality—and offers them to the Buddhas and their stupas, as well as to all bodhisattvas, the community of bhikṣus, and worldly people, giving them all as gifts; he always maintains a gentle countenance and a joyful mind when conversing with others.”
For this reason, when the Buddha walks, he makes low doorways high.

Because in life after life the Bodhisattva provided canopies and latticed pavilions for the Buddha, causing him to dwell and walk beneath them, gazing upon the Buddha with a benevolent mind and further praising the Buddha’s merits—for these reasons, the Buddha emits flames of light such that the sun, moon, and stars all grow dark; none can withstand the Buddha’s radiance, and the majesty of the Buddha’s spiritual power is thus sublime.
The Buddha said:
"When I was a bodhisattva in previous lives, I practiced in this manner for countless lifetimes; I have merely spoken briefly of a small portion of these merits for the sake of others."
Since countless ages past, I have known all my possessions to be impermanent; therefore, I have held them and given them as alms to others.
Such are the merits I have cultivated life after life—deeds that neither Śakra, Brahmā, nor the gods and men can perform—all of which result from the merit practiced in previous lives.

The void may yet be measured; Mount Sumeru may yet be weighed; the waters of the ocean may yet be reckoned; but the meritorious deeds performed by the Buddha and the accumulation of merit throughout his lifetimes cannot be described as weighable or measurable.
If there are those who wholeheartedly recollect the merits of the Buddha, their blessings will be immeasurable; how much more so for those who prostrate and offer praise!
Those who wish to seek the Buddha should likewise cultivate meritorious deeds in this manner.
When the Buddha had finished preaching this sutra, all the bodhisattvas and devas rejoiced; they came forward, prostrated with their heads at the Buddha’s feet, and departed.
*The Sutra on the Fifty Conditions for the Bodhisattva’s Practice of the Body*.
